h1: Eco Inn Lite Ubon Ratchathani — a good-value city-centre hotel within walking distance of Thung Si Mueang and the night market
intro: If you want somewhere central in Ubon for under a thousand baht with everything in walking distance, Eco Inn Lite Ubon Ratchathani comes up again and again. It sits on Si Narong Road in the Thung Si Mueang area — a few minutes' walk from Thung Si Mueang park, Wat Thung Si Mueang and the Rachabut night market, with a 7-Eleven right next door. Rooms are spacious and clean, there are free loaner bikes and free parking, and rates start from around THB 550/night.

body.html: What gets Eco Inn Lite talked about most is its location. The hotel is on Si Narong Road in the Thung Si Mueang area, right in central Ubon, about a 5-minute walk to Thung Si Mueang (the city's central park) and Wat Thung Si Mueang. There's a 7-Eleven next door and restaurants and markets all around, which makes finding food at night easy. Its location sub-score on Trip.com sits around 9.2 — the highest category guests give it.

The hotel opened in 2014 and has 132 rooms. They're simple but larger than you'd expect at this price, tidily furnished, with comfortable beds. Each has a laptop-friendly desk, a fridge, a TV and air conditioning. The Superior King at around 25 sqm is the room guests rate as the best value, while the Standard Twin is smaller. Reception staff are another consistent highlight — helpful, and good at suggesting things to see and where to eat.

"Great location — easy walk to Thung Si Mueang and the markets, with a 7-Eleven right next door. The front desk was lovely and full of sightseeing tips, and the room was bigger than I expected. Great value."

Price is the main reason people choose it. Standard rooms start at around THB 500–730/night depending on the season and festivals. At that level you get a spacious, clean room in the centre of town, plus free loaner bikes, free parking, free Wi-Fi and laundry service. Reviews agree it's good value for anyone visiting Ubon who doesn't want to pay a lot and plans to spend their time out and about rather than in the room.

Now the honest part — Eco Inn Lite isn't a polished new hotel, and there are things to flag. The most common complaint is the air conditioning, which is old and slow to cool; some rooms take a while to get comfortable. The building is showing its age, and one guest likened it to an old motel. Cleanliness can be inconsistent too — some reviews mention mosquitoes or ants, and a bathroom that wasn't fully cleaned on arrival (sorted once staff were told). It's the kind of thing you find at budget prices, but worth knowing up front.

The scores paint a clear picture. Eco Inn Lite sits at around 8.3 on Trip.com across a large number of reviews — broken down into around 9.2 for location, 8.7 for service, 8.3 for cleanliness and 8.1 for amenities. Those numbers match the reviews: location and service are clear strengths, while the rooms and facilities are decent for the price.

Bottom line: Eco Inn Lite suits budget travellers who want a central Ubon base with everything in walking distance, especially during the Candle Festival when Thung Si Mueang is the centre of the action. If you can live with slow AC and a building that isn't new, you get good-value lodging in a great spot for under a thousand baht. If you want a pristine new room or full facilities like a pool, look elsewhere.

A tip from following the reviews here: ask for the Superior King — it's the roomiest and best value. If you check in on a hot afternoon, leave the AC running to cool the room before you head out. And if you're coming for the Candle Festival in July, book several weeks ahead — hotels in the Thung Si Mueang area fill up fast.

faqTitle: FAQ — Eco Inn Lite Ubon Ratchathani

faq.q: Where is Eco Inn Lite and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's on Si Narong Road in the Thung Si Mueang area, central Ubon Ratchathani. It's about a 5-minute walk to Thung Si Mueang park and Wat Thung Si Mueang, and around 10 minutes' walk to the Rachabut night market and Wat Si Ubon Rattanaram. There's a 7-Eleven next door, and Ubon Airport (UBP) is about a 10-minute drive.

faq.q: How much does Eco Inn Lite cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 550/night. A Standard Twin runs around THB 500, a Superior King (about 25 sqm) around THB 600, a Superior Twin around THB 650, and a Deluxe/family room around THB 900. Rates move with the season and festivals — especially the Candle Festival — so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: What are the rooms like, and is there anything to watch out for?
faq.a: Rooms are larger than you'd expect at this price, tidily furnished, with comfortable beds, a desk, fridge and TV. The main things to watch for are old, slow air conditioning in some rooms, an aging building, and cleanliness that can be inconsistent at times — it's worth running the AC before you head out.

faq.q: Who is Eco Inn Lite best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for budget travellers who want a central Ubon base with everything in walking distance, especially during the Candle Festival when Thung Si Mueang is the heart of the action. It's less suited to anyone wanting a pristine new room, a pool or full hotel facilities.

faq.q: Does the hotel have free bikes and parking?
faq.a: Yes, both. Eco Inn Lite offers free loaner bikes, free parking, free Wi-Fi and laundry service. The Thung Si Mueang area is easy to cycle around for the temples and the central park.

faq.q: What review score does Eco Inn Lite have?
faq.a: It sits at around 8.3 on Trip.com — roughly 9.2 for location, 8.7 for service, 8.3 for cleanliness and 8.1 for amenities. Location and service are the clear strengths guests rate highly, while the rooms and facilities are decent for the price.
